papers.title: A Critical Review on Tensile Behavior and Johnson-CookConstitutive Model Calibration of Wire Arc Additive Manufactured Materials
papers.abstract: Wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM) has emerged as a key near-net-shape fabrication route for large-scale aerospace metallic components, offering deposition rates of 3-10 kg/h and material utilization exceeding 90%. However, the non-equilibrium microstructures formed under repeated WAAM thermal cycling — comprising coarse columnar grains, heterogeneous Laves phase, Widmanstatten lamellar alpha, and gradient in-situ aging precipitates — render the mechanical behavior of as-deposited materials fundamentally distinct from wrought counterparts. This disparity gives rise to a systematic 'parameter transplantation fallacy' in engineering simulations that rely on Johnson-Cook (JC) constitutive parameters calibrated from forged stock. The present review systematically examines 69 representative studies published between 2009 and 2026, covering three representative WAAM structural materials: Inconel 718, Ti-6Al-4V (TC4), and 18Ni300 maraging steel. A causal framework linking microstructure formation, tensile behavior, and JC calibration is established. Methodologically, this review proposes a new anisotropy classification taxonomy — texture-precipitate coupling type (IN718), grain boundary-texture type (TC4), and phase distribution-thermal history type (18Ni300) — and builds a cross-material three-tier error priority framework quantifying state-jump error, anisotropy error, and model calibration error. Key findings are: (i) classical JC models exhibit systematic prediction errors of 10-30% for WAAM materials at high strain rates (>1000 s-1) and elevated temperatures (>600 degrees C); (ii) for WAAM IN718, the state-jump error (~42%) far exceeds the anisotropy error (~14%) and model error (<2%), establishing as-deposited-specific parameter databases as the highest-priority research task; (iii) all five JC parameters remain entirely uncharacterized for WAAM as-deposited 18Ni300, representing the most critical knowledge gap in the field. A research roadmap with specific experimental matrices is proposed for near-, mid-, and long-term research directions.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该综述为WAAM Ti-6Al-4V的Johnson-Cook本构模型标定提供了方法论框架，对理解其拉伸行为有参考价值。
llm.why_not_core: It is a review paper covering multiple materials, not original experimental or modeling work specifically on Ti-6Al-4V mechanical/fatigue performance.

summary_zh.motivation: WAAM材料力学行为与锻件差异大，直接套用Johnson-Cook参数存在系统误差，需系统梳理。
summary_zh.method: 综述2009-2026年间69项研究，建立微观结构-拉伸行为-JC标定的因果框架，提出各向异性分类和误差优先级。
summary_zh.result: JC模型对WAAM材料高应变率高温预测误差10-30%，IN718状态跳跃误差约42%，18Ni300全部参数未表征。
summary_zh.validation: 综述方法，基于文献数据统计和误差分析，无新实验。

summary_en.motivation: The non-equilibrium microstructures of WAAM materials render mechanical behavior distinct from wrought, leading to systematic errors when using Johnson-Cook parameters from forged stock.
summary_en.method: This review examines 69 studies (2009-2026) on IN718, Ti-6Al-4V, and 18Ni300, proposing an anisotropy classification taxonomy and a three-tier error priority framework for JC calibration.
summary_en.result: Classical JC models show 10-30% prediction errors for WAAM materials at high strain rates and elevated temperatures; state-jump error dominates in IN718 (~42%), while all five JC parameters for 18Ni300 are uncharacterized.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation; the study is a literature-based review with statistical analysis.
